subject.title: Pause blocked background Claude CLI auth probes

question: Should every five-second Claude auth-status timeout disable background Auto CLI probing for six hours, or should the long cooldown require stronger evidence of a Keychain-blocked subprocess?
rationale: The diff cannot determine whether maintainers prefer aggressive prompt suppression or faster recovery from ordinary CLI slowness, and that choice changes existing provider availability.

options.title: Require blocked-path evidence
options.body: Apply only a short retry delay to generic timeouts and reserve the six-hour cooldown for a confidently diagnosed blocked Keychain path.

options.title: Accept timeout heuristic
options.body: Treat every five-second timeout as likely Keychain blockage and accept up to six hours without background Auto CLI probing.

options.title: Pause for runtime diagnosis
options.body: Hold the PR until packaged-app diagnostics can reliably distinguish blocked Keychain probes from other timeout causes.

recommendation.title: Require blocked-path evidence
recommendation.body: Apply only a short retry delay to generic timeouts and reserve the six-hour cooldown for a confidently diagnosed blocked Keychain path.

likelyOwner.reason: The existing preflight compatibility decision and runtime-proof history make this the strongest available owner for the tradeoff.
